chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man has wealth that is due to his companion. Can he sell him a pearl worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, and delay the payment from him to a specified time?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem. My father instructed me to do so, and I did that.' And he claimed that he asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about it, so he said to him the same.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell an item for a higher price if payment is delayed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* validates the permissibility of *bay' al-mu'ajjal* (deferred payment sale), where the seller retains ownership until full payment, a mechanism often used in *bai' al-kali'* or buy-back structures. The Imam’s reference to his father, Imam Al-Sadiq, underscores the continuity of this commercial ruling within the Ahl al-Bayt’s jurisprudence, distinguishing it from *riba* (usury) by ensuring the price reflects the time value of money without interest on debt. This ruling provides a foundational basis for modern Islamic finance instruments involving asset-backed deferred sales.
